skill.name: security-bluebook-builder
skill.description: Draft structured security Blue Book documentation for sensitive applications.
skill.summary: Create concise Blue Book drafts for application security reviews.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The two static findings are hardcoded GitHub repository links in metadata and documentation. They do not trigger network access or disclose data, and no semantic security issues were found in SKILL.md.

finding_verdicts.reason: The URL is a source repository reference in front matter. It is documentation metadata only and does not cause a network request.
The URL is a Markdown link to the declared source repository. It is informational text, not executable code or data exfiltration.

content.user_title: Build Security Blue Books for Sensitive Apps
content.value_statement: Sensitive applications need clear security documentation before review. This skill helps Codex, Claude, and Claude Code draft structured Blue Book guidance.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of security Blue Book documentation for sensitive applications.
Provides high-level guidance and patterns for security documentation tasks.
Helps frame when to use Blue Book documentation during security work.
Supports structured prompts for application security review notes.
Links to the declared source repository for additional context.
limitations: Does not include scripts, scanners, or automated security tests.
Does not validate security controls against live systems.
Requires user-provided application context for useful output.
Source guidance is brief, so output depth depends on prompt detail.

use_cases.title: Prepare Review Documentation
use_cases.description: Create a Blue Book outline before an architecture or security review.

use_cases.title: Organize App Risk Notes
use_cases.description: Turn sensitive application details into clear security documentation sections.

use_cases.title: Collect Control Evidence
use_cases.description: Draft concise notes about assumptions, controls, and review questions.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Blue Book
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a basic security Blue Book outline for [application]. Include purpose, sensitive data, key risks, and review questions.

prompt_templates.title: Draft App Sections
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft Blue Book sections for [application]. Use this context: [architecture, data types, users, integrations, controls].

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Blue Book draft for gaps. Identify unclear risks, missing controls, weak assumptions, and open security questions.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Final Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a review-ready Blue Book for [application]. Prioritize sensitive data flows, control ownership, residual risk, and approval notes.

output_examples.input: A payments admin portal stores customer identifiers and handles privileged account changes.
output_examples.output: A concise Blue Book outline with scope, sensitive data, trust boundaries, access controls, risks, and reviewer questions.

output_examples.input: An internal analytics app imports production data and exports reports to business teams.
output_examples.output: Security documentation covering data handling, user roles, integration points, control gaps, and follow-up review actions.

best_practices: Provide architecture, data types, user roles, and integrations before asking for a Blue Book.
Mark unknown facts clearly so reviewers can resolve them later.
Use the output as a documentation draft, then validate facts with system owners.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated Blue Book text as completed security approval.
Do not omit sensitive data flows or privileged access paths.
Do not ask for final risk acceptance without providing evidence and owner context.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps draft security Blue Book documentation for sensitive applications.

faq.question: Does it run security scans?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and documentation patterns only.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the application purpose, architecture, data types, users, integrations, and known controls.

faq.question: Can it replace security review?
faq.answer: No. Use the output as a draft for human review and validation.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is live system access required?
faq.answer: No. The skill works from context that the user provides.
